page: Vultr vbm-4c-32gb is a bare metal server belonging to the Bare Metal SSD family. It features an Intel Xeon 1270 processor with 4 physical cores and 8 vCPUs utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 3.8 GHz with dedicated allocation, supported by 32.0 GB of system memory, which equates to 4.0 GB per core. Local storage consists of a 480 GB SSD, and the configuration includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. There are no GPUs bundled with this server.

Benchmark data indicates average performance across most standard compute tasks. The single-core and multi-core stress-ng CPU benchmarks fall into the middle 50% tier, as do the Geekbench single-core and multi-core scores. While the PassMark memory score is in the top 10% tier, memory bandwidth tests reveal a significant performance tradeoff: read-only small block cached bandwidth is average at 494.72 GB/sec, but large block uncached read and write bandwidths drop to the bottom 25% tier at 31.11 GB/sec and 14.73 GB/sec, respectively. Similarly, LLM inference performance is average for small 135M models but drops to poor for medium 7B models.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the dedicated bare metal resources provide predictable compute performance without virtualization overhead. Given the balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and average database operations benchmark of 3949.12 on PassMark, this server is suited for general-purpose workloads, static web serving, software compilation, and lightweight database operations. It is less suitable for memory-intensive large-block data processing or medium-to-large LLM inference tasks.
description: Vultr vbm-4c-32gb is a bare metal server in the Bare Metal SSD family, powered by an Intel Xeon 1270 x86_64 processor with 4 physical cores, 8 vCPUs, and a 3.8 GHz clock speed. It features 32.0 GB of RAM and a 480 GB local SSD, with no GPU acceleration. Performance benchmarks place this server in the middle tier for most compute and database operations, including a PassMark CPU score of 9737.8 and static web serving throughput of 7.05 GB/sec. While its PassMark memory score ranks in the top 10%, uncached large-block memory bandwidth is a notable tradeoff, falling into the bottom 25%. This server provides dedicated, non-virtualized hardware resources, making it a viable option for general-purpose workloads, static web serving, software compilation, and moderate database operations that do not require massive memory bandwidth.
